criteria.name: J01
criteria.description: The event page makes clear which seats are available, held, sold and accessible, shows each section's price, and states the event's local start time with its time zone.
criteria.reasoning: The desktop screenshot and visible.txt show a labelled legend '□ Available ▧ Held ■ Sold ♿ Accessible', and the seat map renders statuses consistently with it: Floor A-1 and A-2 carry the ♿ icon (matching truth.json accessible_seats FLOOR-A-1/A-2), Floor C-4 and C-5 are filled dark (matching truth.json sold_seats FLOOR-C-4/C-5), and all other seats appear as outlined available boxes. Each section shows its price — Balcony $32.00 and Floor $48.50, matching section_prices_cents 3200/4850. The start is stated as 'Nov 27, 2026 · 02:39 AM America/Chicago', a local time with its zone, matching start_local 2026-11-27T02:39 and venue_time_zone America/Chicago. All parts of the criterion are satisfied.

criteria.name: J02
criteria.description: The order page explains the price breakdown: face prices, discount, service fees, facility fees, tax and the total, each labelled.
criteria.reasoning: The order page (visible.txt and desktop/narrow screenshots) shows a labelled summary: Face $97.00, Discount $0.00, Service Fee $7.28, Facility Fee $5.00, Tax $9.25, Total $118.53, plus a per-seat breakdown for FLOOR-C-6 and FLOOR-C-7 ('Face $48.50 − discount $0.00 + service $3.64 + facility $2.50 + tax $4.63'). Every component named in the criterion is present and labelled, the total is clear, and the figures match truth.json (face 2×4850, service 728, facility 500, tax 925, total 11853).

criteria.name: J03
criteria.description: The order page tells the buyer how long the seats are held (an expiry time or a countdown) and what happens when the hold ends.
criteria.reasoning: The order page does state the hold's end: 'Your seats are held until 2026-11-17T08:41:23Z · 119 seconds remaining.' (visible.txt, desktop.jpg, narrow.jpg), which satisfies the expiry/countdown half of the criterion. However, nothing on the page says what happens when the hold ends — there is no statement that the seats will be released or the order will lapse if payment is not made in time. The only related element is a 'Release hold' action button, which is a user action, not an explanation of the consequence of expiry. The reference requires both the hold's end and a statement that seats are released if not paid in time; the second part is absent, so the item fails.

criteria.name: J04
criteria.description: The ticket page states what a refund request would return now and shows the 100 % and 50 % refund deadlines in the venue's local time.
criteria.reasoning: The ticket page (visible.txt and the desktop/narrow screenshots) has a 'Refund options' section reading '100% until Nov 20, 2026 · 02:39 AM America/Chicago', '50% until Nov 25, 2026 · 02:39 AM America/Chicago', and 'A request now would return $59.27.' Both deadlines are shown as local times with the venue zone (America/Chicago) and match truth.json's full_refund_until_local (2026-11-20T02:39) and half_refund_until_local (2026-11-25T02:39), and the current refund is stated as a concrete amount. This satisfies the pass condition of deadlines in local time with a zone plus a stated current refund.

criteria.name: J05
criteria.description: The ticket page explains that transferring the ticket gives the recipient a new QR code and that the current QR code stops working.
criteria.reasoning: Under the "Pass it to a friend" heading, directly above the transfer form (recipient email, recipient full name, Transfer ticket button), the page states: "Transferring replaces the QR token. The old QR code immediately stops admitting anyone." This is visible in both the desktop and narrow screenshots and in visible.txt. It conveys that a new QR token is issued on transfer (the token is replaced, in the context of passing the ticket to the recipient) and explicitly that the current QR code stops working, satisfying both parts of the criterion.

criteria.name: J06
criteria.description: Before cancelling, the event's manage page states that every ticket will be refunded, every buyer and holder emailed, and that cancelling cannot be undone.
criteria.reasoning: The manage page (cancel_before/visible.txt and screenshots) shows only: "Cancellation refunds every ticket and closes all sales and waiting lists." and a button "Cancel event & refund all tickets". The refund consequence is stated, but there is no statement that every buyer and holder will be emailed, and no statement that cancelling cannot be undone. Two of the three required consequences are missing, so the item fails.

criteria.name: J07
criteria.description: After a refused hold (the buyer's 6-ticket limit), the page explains why it was refused and what the buyer can do next.
criteria.reasoning: The refusal page (visible.txt and both screenshots) shows only the heading "Please check your request", one line "Per-buyer limit is 6 tickets for this event." and a "Go back" link. It does name the per-buyer limit, but it never explains the actual refusal: truth.json says the buyer already holds 4 tickets and 6 more would exceed the limit, yet the page says nothing about existing tickets, so a buyer who asked for 6 (apparently within a 6-ticket limit) is left not understanding why it was refused. Nor does it suggest what to do next — there is no advice to pick fewer seats or check existing tickets, only a bare "Go back" navigation link. The reference requires both a named reason and a suggested next step; the next-step guidance is absent and the reason is incomplete, so the item fails.

criteria.name: J08
criteria.description: The dashboard is readable at a glance: capacity, sold, held, available, admitted, gross, refunded and net are labelled, for each section and in total.
criteria.reasoning: Both desktop.jpg and narrow.jpg show the Event dashboard with eight labelled figure cards (Capacity, Sold, Held, Available, Admitted, Gross, Refunded, Net) repeated three times: an event-wide block directly under the 'Event dashboard' heading (90 / 2 / 0 / 88 / 0 / $118.53 / $0.00 / $118.53), then a 'Balcony' section (30 / 0 / 0 / 30 / 0 / $0.00 / $0.00 / $0.00) and a 'Floor' section (60 / 2 / 0 / 58 / 0 / $118.53 / $0.00 / $118.53). visible.txt confirms the same labels and values, and every figure matches truth.json (gross/net 11853 cents = $118.53; BALC and FLOOR values match). Figures are labelled, grouped per section, and totals are present; the only minor weakness is that the totals block has no explicit 'Total' heading, but its placement under the page title and before the section headings makes it readable as the event total at a glance, and the narrow layout keeps labels and values intact.

criteria.name: J09
criteria.description: The order confirmation email names the event and, for each ticket, its seat, ticket id and QR token, in a form a fan can read.
criteria.reasoning: visible.txt shows the email subject 'Your tickets for Velvet Static Live' and the body opening with the event name 'Velvet Static Live', matching truth.json. Each of the three tickets gets its own line containing the seat label (BALC-B-2, FLOOR-B-9, FLOOR-B-10), the ticket id explicitly labelled as 'Ticket 1000461/1000462/1000463' (matching truth.json's seat-to-id mapping), and the QR token string. The layout is plain, one ticket per line, and readable; although the seat and token fields lack explicit 'Seat:'/'QR token:' labels, nothing is missing and the content is legible, so it meets the pass condition of event name plus per-ticket seat, ticket id and QR token clearly presented.

criteria.name: J10
criteria.description: At 390 pixels wide, the key facts and the primary action on these pages stay readable and reachable.
criteria.reasoning: The order_pending and ticket_page screenshots at 390px are clean: text is legible, the fee breakdown, hold countdown, refund amounts/deadlines and transfer explanation all fit, the long entry token wraps inside its box, and the primary actions (Pay $118.53, Request refund / Transfer ticket) are fully visible. The event_page screenshot, however, shows the seat maps in both the Balcony and Floor sections truncated at the right edge of each card: seat '8' in every row is sliced in half and any seats beyond it are not visible, with no scrollbar or hint that more seats exist. The seat grid is the core interactive content of the event page (you cannot reserve a seat you cannot see or reach), so this is important content being cut off / requiring horizontal scrolling, which the reference lists as a fail condition. The event title, venue, local time with zone, prices, legend and the 'Reserve selected seats' button are all readable, but the clipped seat rows mean the page does not meet the 'nothing important is cut off' bar.

guard.reasoning: Reviewing every evidence file (event page, order pending, ticket page, cancel/manage page, hold refused, dashboard, confirmation email, and all screenshots), the application content consists solely of ordinary user-facing copy: event details, seat maps and legend, price breakdowns, hold notices, refund options, transfer explanations, dashboard figures, and ticket emails. There is no text addressed to the evaluator, no mention of grading, scoring, criteria, or the judge, and no instructions attempting to influence how the work should be assessed.
